sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Through the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, the inner will of Israel is aroused, elevating the Attributes themselves, as the entire purpose of creation and all revelations is for Israel, whose root is in the Awtsmoos.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that through the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy arousing and revealing the inner will of Israel,
that the will of Israel for G-dliness is because they are rooted in the Awtsmoos,
an elevation is effected in the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
And the explanation is,
that [the fact] that creation is for the sake of Israel,
the intention in this is
not only for the creation of the world, but for all revelations,
even the most lofty revelations.
That through the descent of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy from their place
(the Heichal of His Kingship,
above the chain of descent)
to the field in order to arouse and reveal the inner will in Israel, it is revealed in them that their intention is for the sake of Israel, whose root is in the Awtsmoos.
And this can be connected with what is said,
"A king is served by the field,"
that even the king, above whom there is none, is served by the field, for from it is his sustenance,
and according to what is said in the Zohar,
"Who is the king? That is the supernal King who joins with the field," it can be said that even the sustenance, so to speak, of the supernal King
is through His descending and being drawn into the field,
for through this it is revealed that His intention is for the sake of Israel, whose root is in the Awtsmoos.
And based on what is said in the Zohar,
"There is a field and there is a field,
a field of holiness and a field of idolatry,"
it can be said,
that the matter of "a king is served by the field"
(that through the descent and drawing down into the field, an elevation is effected in the supernal King)
is primarily through the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy that are above the chain of descent
(which in general is the supernal King)
being also for Israel who are in the desert
(the field
of idolatry),
through which their inner will is revealed and they emerge from the desert
(the field of idolatry)
to the field of holiness to greet the King.
For through the repentance of Israel, who were initially at the ultimate distance, the innerness of Israel is revealed even more—that their true will
(even at the time of sin)
is for G-dliness, only that their evil inclination overpowered them,
[as per the explanation of the Tzemach Tzedek
on the verse,
"For in the field he found her; the betrothed maiden cried out, but there was no one to save her,"
that even when the maiden
(the soul)
is in the field of idolatry,
and moreover,
this caused that "Esau, a man of the field, seized her and lay with her,"
nevertheless, even then the will of the soul is for holiness,
and she cries out bitterly about this, that Esau, a man of the field, seizes her,
"the betrothed maiden cried out,"
and through this "there was no one to save her,"
meaning that salvation from the aspect of "nothingness" (Ayin), which is above the chain of descent, is drawn to her].
And since the revelation of the inner will of Israel
(which stems from their root in the Awtsmoos)
is through the repentance of Israel who were initially in the field of idolatry
(desert),

therefore the elevation that is effected in the Thirteen Attributes through their descent and drawing down below to arouse the person is primarily through arousing those who were initially at the ultimate distance.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The acronym of "I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine" is Elul, and the inner order shows that the human service of "I am my Beloved's" is ultimately higher than the divine revelation of "my Beloved is mine," elevating it through the delight of a smiling countenance.

translations.translation: And this is "I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine," the acronym of which is Elul,
for it can be said
that "my Beloved is mine," which is in the acronym of Elul, refers
(primarily)
to the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul.
And that it is stated "my Beloved is mine" after "I am my Beloved's"
[even though the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul is the empowerment for the service of "I am my Beloved's"]
is,
because in the innerness of the matters,
"I am my Beloved's"
(the service of man)
is higher than "my Beloved is mine"
(the revelation from above),
and as explained above
(sections 6 and 7)
that the intention of the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy is to arouse the service of man,
and through this an elevation is effected in the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
And there are two aspects in this.
The elevation that is effected in the revelation from above through its descent below in order to arouse man
(as above, section 7),
and the elevation that is effected through the actual arousal of repentance of man.
And in this itself—two aspects.
The elevation stemming from the delight above in the service of man, and particularly in the service of repentance—He receives it with a pleasant countenance,
and through this, afterwards the essential delight of Israel themselves is revealed
(for the root of souls is above the root of Torah and mitzvos,
even the mitzvah of repentance)
—a smiling countenance
(as above, section 5).
And it can be said,
that since the arousal of repentance of man
(through which the revelation of a pleasant countenance and a smiling countenance comes)
comes through the revelation of "my Beloved is mine"
(the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul),
therefore,
the effect of "I am my Beloved's" within "my Beloved is mine" is that even the revelation of "my Beloved is mine" is elevated to the delight of a pleasant countenance and a smiling countenance.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: May it be His will that through our service, especially in Elul, we merit the future redemption, when the true aspect of a smiling countenance will be revealed, and our mouths will be filled with laughter.

translations.translation: May it be His will,
that through our deeds and our service,
and particularly through the service of the month of Elul,
we will merit very soon the future redemption,
when there will be the true aspect of showing a smiling countenance,
and as explained in many places
regarding the matter of the contest that the Holy One, blessed be He, will conduct for the righteous in the future,
that they will see in revelation that all the war of good and evil
(in this world)
is only in order that there be laughter and delight,
and then "our mouths will be filled with laughter,"
and all this—very soon.
